ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the ex-works price of the vehicle - excluding the vehicle battery - minus the value of components incorporated into the vehicle not originating in the Union and the ex-works price of the vehicle – excluding the vehicle battery – is at least 70%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 80%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 75%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 75%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 75%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery – non-originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of the vehicle - excluding the battery - does not exceed 30 %;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b a (new)
ev.amended: (ba)at least 80% of the ex-works price of the vehicle, excluding the battery, corresponds to Union value added. For the purposes of this point, research and development, design and engineering activities, including related intellectual property, royalties and licence fees, shall be considered as originating in the Union only where they are carried out in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b a (new)
ev.amended: (ba)the ratio between R&D and labor costs of eligible type approved vehicles shall be at least 70 % invested in the EU;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b a (new)
ev.amended: (ba)the vehicle's tyres originate in the Union;
ev.justification: The same requirement should apply to electric vehicles supported through public schemes and corporate fleet incentives, to ensure consistency with public procurement.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: deleted

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least four main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union, as of 1 January 2029. This threshold shall be increased to at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union, as of 1 January 2032;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least one main specific component of batteries, among which assembly, cathode active materials, battery management systems (BMS), originating in the Union or in the United Kingdom;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three components of batteries, among which a main specific component of batteries, the battery cells and the binders, originating in the Union;
ev.justification: Binders are an essential component of battery cells, ensuring their integrity and performance. Union manufacturers can fully meet EU demand for binders and are expected to do so for at least the next decade. Excluding binders from Union origin requirements would leave a critical upstream segment unaddressed and, in light of ongoing distortive trade practices, undermine the objective of safeguarding existing EU manufacturing capacity.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least four main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells and the cathode active material, originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains the binders and at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains the binders and at least four components of batteries, among which the battery cells originating in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains the battery cells, the binders, as well as one main specific component originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: deleted

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle's traction battery contains at least seven main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material and the battery management system and at least two of the following five components: the separators (including separator covers), the electrolyte, the battery housing and support structures, or the thermal management components, originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, including calcination and active material formation, the binders and the battery management system, originating in the Union; and at least 20% of the lithium, 15% of nickel, and 10% of phosphate used should be low-carbon and of Union Origin;
ev.justification: Annex II should include battery-grade nickel sulphate, lithium hydroxide and phosphate alongside steel, aluminium and concrete. Including these critical materials would support resilient European value chains, low-carbon production and Union-origin supply, while reducing carbon leakage and unnecessary processing outside Europe. Minimum content requirements of 15% for nickel sulphate, 20% for lithium hydroxide and 10% for phosphate would provide a realistic demand signal aligned with European refining capacity.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five components of batteries, among which a main specific component of batteries, the battery cells, the cathode active material, including calcination and active material formation, the binders and the battery management system, originating in the Union; and at least 20% by mass of the lithium shall be mined, processed or recycled within the Union;
ev.justification: Binders are an essential component of battery cells, ensuring their integrity and performance. Union manufacturers can fully meet EU demand for binders and are expected to do so for at least the next decade. Excluding binders from Union origin requirements would leave a critical upstream segment unaddressed and, in light of ongoing distortive trade practices, undermine the objective of safeguarding existing EU manufacturing capacity.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains the binders and at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union; and at least 20% of the relevant strategic raw materials should be mined, processed or recycled within the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains the battery cells, the binders, the cathode active material, the battery management system and one additional main specific component, originating in the Union, and at least 20% of the lithium contained in the battery have been extracted, processed or recycled within the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least four main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union, as of 1 January 2029, and five such components as of 1 January 2032;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains the binders and at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material (including calcination and active material formation), and the battery management system, originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union or in the United Kingdom;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d a (new)
ev.amended: (da)the vehicle’s traction battery contains the battery cells, the binders, the cathode active material, at least 20% of precursors of the cathode active material, at least 20% of the anode active material, the battery management system and one additional main specific component, originating in the Union, and at least 30% of the lithium contained in the battery have been extracted, processed or recycled within the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d b (new)
ev.amended: (db)the recycled contents of lithium, nickel and cobalt contained in the active materials of the traction battery corresponding to the respective minimum share laid down in Article 8 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 50%;
ev.amended: deleted

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total added value of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total added value of all e-powertrain components is at least 50%. For the purpose of calculating Union content in vehicles and vehicle components, Union-origin value incorporated throughout the supply chain, including tier-two and tier-three components and subcomponents, should be appropriately recognised and traceable. This should include cast parts incorporated into higher-tier components;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components, including electrical steels, originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 80%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components, including electrical steels, originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 80%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of main electronic systems originating in the Union or in the United Kingdom, and the total ex-works price of all main electronic systems is equal to or greater than 50%.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components including software originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 50%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of the e-powertrain originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of the e-powertrain is equal to or greater than 50%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 60 %;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is equal to or greater than 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components non-originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of the e-powertrain does not exceed 50%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e a (new)
ev.amended: (ea)as of [OP: please insert date = two years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation], the tyres the vehicle has been fitted with are of Union origin as of delivery and, in the case of M1- and N1-category vehicles, are at least class B for fuel efficiency and class B for wet grip performance within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2020/740;
ev.justification: Subsidised and corporate vehicles should be subject to the same original fitting requirement.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point e a (new)
ev.amended: (ea)the ratio between the ex-works price of permanent magnets originating in the Union that are used in e-powertrain and the total ex-works price of all permanent magnets in e-powertrain is at least 50%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f
ev.original: (f)the ratio between the total ex-works price of main electronic systems originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all main electronic systems is equal to or greater than 50%.
ev.amended: (f)the ratio between the total ex-works price of main electronic systems originating in the Union, including software, and the total ex-works price of all main electronic systems is equal to or greater than 20 % as of [OP: please insert date = three years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation], 35 % as of [OP: please insert date = five years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation] and 50 % as of [OP: please insert date = seven years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation], subject to Article 16(2c).
ev.justification: For the sake of consistency with Part I, the same phased approach should apply to public support schemes and corporate vehicles.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)vehicles belonging to category M2 or M3 as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/858 shall be exempt from the requirement set out in point a) if the total ex-works price of materials not of Union - excluding the vehicle battery – does not exceed 20% of the total ex-works price of the vehicle – excluding the vehicle battery.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)at least x% in accordance with Article 8(2) of Regulation 2023/1542 of the cobalt, lead, lithium and nickel contained in the active materials of the vehicle’s traction battery is recycled content recovered and refined in the EU.
ev.justification: The EU Batteries Regulation establishes binding recycled content for cobalt, lead, lithium or nickel for batteries placed on the EU market from 2031 onwards. Meanwhile Annex III of the IAA on electric vehicles proposes Union-origin requirements for electric vehicles and, consequently, for certain battery components. The unfortunate current situation is that the IAA refers to union-origin, but not recycled content, while the batteries regulation refers to recycled content, but not union origin. In search of consistency this amendment on 'recycled in Europe' is introduced.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least 20% of precursor cathode active materials (including battery-grade transition-metal precursor compounds), and at least 10% of anode active materials, originating in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)the vehicle’s critical glazing components (windshields, rear and side windows made of glass, including rooftop glass installations) originate in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – subparagraph 1 (new)
ev.amended: The requirement set out in point (c) shall apply from [OP: please insert date 12 months after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.justification: To allow industry sufficient time to adapt to the new rules, the amendment extends the period from 6 to 12 months before the requirement for three battery components to be of Union origin applies.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)the ratio between R&D and labor costs of eligible type approved vehicles shall be at least 70 % invested in the EU.
ev.justification: European OEMs account for a significant portion of total R&D investment, which is not addressed in the current proposal. At the same time, this is the only activity outside of manufacturing that manufacturers can directly influence. Furthermore, OEMs account for a significant percentage of European jobs, which, in the case of manufacturers, are rated above average.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)the monitoring of the actual employment and value creation effects within the European automotive supplier industry.
ev.justification: Assessment criteria should not be limited to physical production and resource metrics alone, but must equally account for employment and value creation generated across the European automotive supplier industry. Research, development and engineering are essential parts of the automotive value chain which should not be looked over, as monitoring these elements would provide a more comprehensive picture of the economic impact of the Union origin requirements

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)the vehicle’s traction battery contains the precursors of cathode active materials originating in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f b (new)
ev.amended: (fb)at least 20% of the lithium, nickel, cobalt and natural graphite contained in the vehicle’s traction battery shall be mined and processed in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f c (new)
ev.amended: (fc)the recycled content of the vehicle’s traction battery required under Article 8 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 originates in the Union and is verified in accordance with the rules on the calculation and verification of recycled content adopted pursuant to that Article.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point f c (new)
ev.amended: (fc)at least 20 % of the lithium, nickel, cobalt and natural graphite in the vehicle’s traction battery is extracted, processed or recycled in the Union or an overseas country and territory listed in Annex II TFEU.
ev.justification: The overseas countries and territories can help to safeguard the resilience and security of the Union’s supply chains for raw materials of strategic interest. For the sake of consistency with the corresponding provision in Part I, raw materials extracted, processed or recycled in those countries and territories should therefore be taken into account.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 a (new)
ev.amended: By way of derogation from point (a), until 1 January 2035, vehicles of categories N2, N3, M2 and M3, as defined in Article 4(1) of Regulation (EU) 2018/858, shall be considered to comply with that point where the vehicle is assembled in a country with which the Union has concluded an agreement establishing a free trade area, by or on behalf of a heavy-duty vehicle manufacturer established in the Union, and where that manufacturer, either itself or through an established network of suppliers and subcontractors, participates in a fully integrated value chain with that country which was already established on the date of entry into force of this Regulation.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 b (new)
ev.amended: For this annex, non-road mobile machinery shall be considered as equivalent to a ‘vehicle’. The same provisions apply.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date three years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended:
The requirements set out in points d) apply from once a Commission impact assessment has been carried out on the capacity of European battery value chains, considering: available battery cell chemistry; maturity of the battery ecosystem (including processing capacity, competitive pricing, etc); different battery cell requirements (chemistry and cell format) for different applications. A requirement for the mandatory use of European battery cells should enter into force no earlier than 2031.
Where requirements under this Annex apply, appropriate Union or national support measures, including financial incentives, should be made available to offset additional costs linked to the localization of battery supply chains and to preserve affordability for Union consumers. Such support measures shall include adequate operating expenditure (OPEX) funding for Union battery cell manufacturers from 2028 onwards.
The review of this Regulation referred to in Article 29 shall assess the availability in the Union of the battery components covered by this Annex and, where necessary, propose adjustments to ensure that the requirements remain feasible and proportionate.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date three years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended:
The requirements set out in points e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation] for vehicles of categories M1 and N1.
The requirements set out in point c) apply from 2032 for vehicles of categories M1 and N1.
The requirements set out in point d) apply from 2035 for vehicles of categories M1 and N1.
The requirements set out in points c), d), e) and f) apply from 2035 for vehicles of categories N2, N3, M2 and M3.
Twelve months before the date of application of each of the requirements set out in points (c) to (f), the Commission shall assess whether sufficient volumes of the relevant Union-origin components – and, in the case of points (c) and (d), traction batteries incorporating the required combination of those components – are commercially available to vehicle manufacturers.
That assessment shall consider actual production output in the Union, validated automotive-grade capacity, available battery chemistries and formats, processing capacity, binding supply commitments, delivery conditions, and the price differential compared with equivalent non-Union products. Announced or nominal production capacity shall not, by itself, constitute evidence of sufficient availability.
Where the assessment demonstrates that insufficient availability, inadequate technical suitability, or a disproportionate price premium would make compliance excessively difficult, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act postponing the date of application of the relevant requirement or establishing an appropriate temporary derogation.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date three years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended: The requirement relating to the ratio for e-powertrain components and the requirement relating to the ratio for main electronic systems apply from [OP: please insert date three years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation]. The requirement that the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material and the battery management system, originating in the Union, applies from the date from which point (d) of Part I applies pursuant to paragraph 4 of that Part. For vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3, the requirement that the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union, applies from [OP: please insert date 2 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.justification: This Part lists its requirements with two points lettered (a) and no point (f), so a reference to points (d), (e) and (f) does not identify the requirements intended. Referring to the requirements by their content gives legal certainty and aligns the timing for cathode active materials, and for battery cells in buses and trucks, with Part I, so that support for fleet renewal follows the same rules as procurement.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date three years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended:

ev.amended:
Upon request of a vehicle manufacturer, all PEV or OVC-HEV from that vehicle manufacturer can be considered compliant, for a period of twelve months, with the Union origin requirements if the manufacturer demonstrates that all PEV or OVC-HEV compliant with the Union origin requirements that were assembled by that vehicle manufacturer during the period comprised between 1 January and 31 December (included) of the previous year represent a percentage equal or greater than 80% of the total number of PEV or OVC-HEV from the same vehicle manufacturer that were registered within the Union in the same period.​
Where one or more vehicle manufacturers are subsidiaries of an automotive group, the parent company of the group that exercises control over the subsidiaries shall be entitled to submit the application pursuant to the preceding paragraph. In such case, all PEV or OVC-HEV of all subsidiaries can be considered compliant for a period of twelve months with the Union origin requirements if the parent company demonstrates that the total number of all PEV or OVC-HEV vehicles compliant with the Union origin requirements that were assembled by all subsidiaries during the period comprised between 1 January and 31 December (included) of the previous year represent a percentage equal or greater than at least 80% of the total number of PEV or OVC-HEV from all subsidiaries that were registered within the Union in the same period.
By way of derogation, a vehicle manufacturer or the parent company of the group that exercises control over the subsidiaries may request a reduction of the 80% threshold by up to 10 percentage points, where it demonstrates that expenditure on research and development carried out in the Union in the previous calendar year exceeded 1% of the gross annual revenue generated by its Union asset.
ev.justification: The European automotive industry is strongly export-oriented: over one-third of EU-made cars are sold in non-EU markets, generating tens of billions of euros in value added drawn from outside Europe. Exports and direct OEM R&D spending should be integrated into the IAA through a voluntary and optional company-level compliance mechanism.

The requirement set out in point (b) shall apply from 2032.
By way of derogation to the requirements set out above, small electric vehicles of subcategory M1E, as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/858, shall include the following Union origin requirements:
1. The vehicle is assembled within the Union;

Compliance with Union origin requirements for small electric vehicles of subcategory M1E, as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/858, through criteria set in point 2(b) shall only be possible as of 2032.
Upon request of a vehicle manufacturer, all PEV, OVC-HEV or FCV from that vehicle manufacturer can be considered compliant, for a period of twelve months, with the Union origin requirements if the manufacturer demonstrates that all PEV, OVC-HEV or FCV compliant with the Union origin requirements that were assembled by that vehicle manufacturer during the period comprised between 1 January and 31 December (included) of the previous year represent a percentage equal or greater than 70% of the total number of PEV, OVC-HEV or FCV from the same vehicle manufacturer that were registered within the Union in the same period.
Where one or more vehicle manufacturers are subsidiaries of an automotive group, the parent company of the group that exercises control over the subsidiaries shall be entitled to submit the application pursuant to the preceding paragraph. In such case, all PEV, OVC-HEV or FCV of all subsidiaries can be considered compliant for a period of twelve months with the Union origin requirements if the parent company demonstrates that the total number of all PEV, OVC-HEV or FCV vehicles compliant with the Union origin requirements that were assembled by all subsidiaries during the period comprised between 1 January and 31 December (included) of the previous year represent a percentage equal or greater than at least 70% of the total number of PEV, OVC-HEV or FCV from all subsidiaries that were registered within the Union in the same period.

ev.original: Super credits for small zero-emission vehicles
ev.amended: Super credits for zero-emission vehicles
ev.justification: The IAA should pair its requirements with incentives and additional funding that at least partially offset the increased costs of localising production, creating a genuine business case for manufacturing in the EU. At present, the most dependable incentive for cars and vans is the super-credit under the CO2 Regulation. Because it cannot be modified, cancelled, or withdrawn at Member State discretion, it offers manufacturers a degree of planning certainty the other mechanisms lack. Public support can be withdrawn by Member States or never granted in the first place. Furthermore, the proposal allows Member States to opt out of applying "Made in EU" provisions to public procurement and support schemes altogether, via the “escape clause” if it proves disproportionate costs. Effectively asking manufacturers to buy European while declining to hold public sector to the same standard. A manufacturer that has invested in local production and supply chain may see no reward for it, should a public authority simply choose to use that opt-out. Therefore, Extend the super-credit mechanism to other categories, including a super-credit of 1.3 to ALL zero-emission vehicles "Made in EU," not only small. ***For cars: 1) for small zero-emission vehicles “Made in EU” a super-credit of 1.5; 2) for all zero-emission vehicles “Made in EU” a super-credit of 1.3; 3) for small zero-emission vehicles (regardless of origin) a super-credit of 1.3.For vans: 1) for zero-emission vehicles “Made in EU” a super-credit of 1.5; 2) for all zero-emission vehicles regardless of origin a super-credit of 1.3.***

ev.original: (9)The automotive industry is a cornerstone of the Union economy. With a view to delivering on the Union’s climate policy objectives, over the past years, the European automotive industry has been investing heavily in the development of cleaner vehicles and innovative components. Electric vehicles and electric vehicle components, including traction batteries, e-powertrain components and electronic systems, are essential technologies for advancing the decarbonisation of road transport. However, as a result of costs disadvantage and the transformation of the value chain with an increasing value share for batteries, e-powertrain and electronics, the level of Union content in vehicles produced in the Union is decreasing. It is no longer possible to postpone effective measures to avoid the risk of local production being displaced. In the absence of such measures, the current circumstances would lead to a full reliance on third countries for key vehicle components. That would be a serious threat to the Union’s economic security and future resilience, as well as for its climate goals.
ev.amended: (9)The automotive industry is a cornerstone of the Union economy and a major source of skilled industrial employment. With a view to delivering on the Union’s climate policy objectives, over the past years, the European automotive industry has been investing heavily in the development of cleaner vehicles and innovative components. Electric vehicles and electric vehicle components, including traction batteries, e-powertrain components and electronic systems, are essential technologies for advancing the decarbonisation of road transport. However, the sector is currently facing a severe structural crisis, marked by significant job losses across the Union and by the closure or restructuring of manufacturing sites in several Member States. This crisis is aggravated by costs disadvantage and the transformation of the value chain with an increasing value share for batteries, e-powertrain and electronics, resulting in a decreasing level of Union content in vehicles produced in the Union. It is no longer possible to postpone effective measures to avoid the risk of local production being displaced. In line with other Union policies, dedicated demand-side measures supporting zero-emission vehicles and their components originating in the Union are essential to strengthen Union automotive value chains, halt further job losses and reduce the Union’s growing dependence on third countries for key vehicle components. Without such measures, the Union risks further loss of industrial capacity and full reliance on third countries, undermining its economic security, resilience and climate goals.

(9a)Activities relating to the recovery of materials produce secondary raw materials that are used both upstream and downstream across the value chains of the energy-intensive industries, of the automotive sector and of net-zero technologies. Recycled steel scrap contributes directly to the decarbonisation of the Union's steel industry, recycled aluminium is essential to the aluminium value chain, and recycled critical raw materials play a growing role in the manufacturing of batteries, motors and net-zero technology components. Activities relating to the recovery of materials are therefore of strategic importance for the resilience of Union industrial supply chains, for the achievement of the Union's circular economy objectives, and for the reduction of industrial greenhouse gas emissions. The definition of low-carbon products under this Regulation should fully recognise the contribution of recycled materials to decarbonisation objectives, including through taking into accounted the avoidance of greenhouse gas emissions associated with the use of secondary raw materials in production processes.

ev.original: (19)Demand-side measures should focus on establishing low-carbon requirements for steel, cement and aluminium used in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles, where appropriate, since those sectors are the most energy-intensive industries. Targeted Union wide demand-side measures can help create lead markets for low-carbon and Union-produced energy-intensive industrial products, supporting decarbonisation while strengthening the Union’s industrial base.
ev.amended: (19)Demand-side measures should focus on establishing Union-origin requirements and low-carbon requirements for steel, cement, aluminium and plastics used in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles, since those sectors are the most energy-intensive industries. Targeted Union wide demand-side measures can help create lead markets for low-carbon and Union-produced energy-intensive industrial products, supporting decarbonisation while strengthening the Union’s industrial base.

ev.original: (20)Downstream sectors that account for a large share of demand for certain energy-intensive materials, such as the construction and automotive sectors, should be prioritised under this Regulation when establishing low-carbon requirements, Union origin requirements, or both. That is particularly appropriate given that such sectors are significantly subject to public procurement and support schemes, while the share of energy-intensive input in total production value is relatively small and therefore minimises the impact of any price premium.
ev.amended: (20)Downstream sectors that account for a large share of demand for certain energy-intensive materials, such as the construction and automotive sectors, should be prioritised under this Regulation when establishing low-carbon requirements and Union origin requirements. That is particularly appropriate given that such sectors are significantly subject to public procurement and support schemes, while the share of energy-intensive input in total production value is relatively small and therefore minimises the impact of any price premium.

(24a)Member States should design public support schemes, in a way that they contribute to the objectives of strengthening the Union’s strategic industrial value chains through the Union-origin requirements and low-carbon content requirements, as well as compliance with applicable social and labour law. When designing such public support schemes, Member States should design public support schemes in a manner that discourages the relocation of manufacturing activities supported outside the territory of the Union. To provide legal certainty and ensure the effective use of public funds, where such relocation nevertheless takes place within five years from the date on which the support is granted, or within three years in the case of SMEs, the support granted should be recovered by the competent authority... Member States should apply these requirements to public support schemes accounting for at least 90% of the total national budget allocated to schemes that benefit households or companies and that primarily aim to support the construction or renovation of buildings for residential and commercial purposes and infrastructure and the lease and purchase of motor vehicles for civil purposes, and accounting for 100% of the total national budget allocated to other forms of public intervention and financial support for corporate vehicles.

ev.original: (66)The provisions on public procurement laid down in this Regulation should build on the provisions of Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 on resilience; and complement them by introducing additional requirements for battery energy storage systems, solar photovoltaic technologies, heat pumps, onshore and offshore wind technologies, electrolysers and nuclear fission energy technologies. Such additional requirements should ensure that a certain share of the products and their main specific components originate in the Union. That approach should ensure sufficient diversification while strengthening strategic manufacturing capacity and technological sovereignty within the Union. The system for verification of compliance with the requirements should limit the administrative burden and align with common public procurement practice as well as the existing system of verification of compliance under Regulation (EU) 2024/1735. It should therefore rely on a self-declaration by economic operators.
ev.amended: (66)The provisions on public procurement laid down in this Regulation should build on the provisions of Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 on resilience; and complement them by introducing additional requirements for battery energy storage systems, solar photovoltaic and solar thermal technologies, heat pumps, onshore and offshore wind technologies, electrolysers and nuclear fission energy technologies and electric charging technologies. Such additional requirements should ensure that a certain share of the products and their main specific components originate in the Union. That approach should ensure sufficient diversification while strengthening strategic manufacturing capacity and technological sovereignty within the Union. The system for verification of compliance with the requirements should limit the administrative burden and align with common public procurement practice as well as the existing system of verification of compliance under Regulation (EU) 2024/1735. It should therefore rely on a self-declaration by economic operators.

ev.original: (70)Businesses and households are an essential part of the demand for net-zero technologies in the Union. Public support schemes designed to support consumer demand for such products are important tools for strengthening the Union’s economic security and accelerating the green transition. In order to build on the provisions of Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 on resilience, it is necessary to complement those provisions introducing additional requirements for battery energy storage systems, solar photovoltaic technologies and heat pumps. Such additional requirements should ensure that certain main specific components and, in some cases, the whole final product, originate in the Union. That approach is in line with the general objective of support schemes to promote socially-desirable outcomes, in view of making progress on the ambitions of the European Pillar of Social Rights as well as environmental and climate objectives. Furthermore, it should ensure sufficient diversification while strengthening strategic manufacturing capacity and technological sovereignty within the Union. Public authorities in charge of support schemes should have the possibility either to condition the eligibility of the scheme to the fulfilment of the requirements, or to grant additional financial compensation when the requirements are fulfilled. In the latter case, the additional financial compensation should have an incentivising effect. However, if State aid is involved, the additional financial compensation should not exceed the applicable maximum aid intensity.

ev.original: For auctions published after [OP: Please insert the date = 3 years after entry into force of this Regulation], the battery energy storage system shall originate in the Union and contain battery cells, a battery management system as well as one additional main specific components that originate in the Union.
ev.amended: For auctions published after [OP: Please insert the date = 3 years after entry into force of this Regulation], the battery energy storage system shall originate in the Union and contain battery cells, a battery management system, cathode active materials as well as one additional main specific components that originate in the Union. At least 20% of the relevant strategic raw materials used shall be mined, processed or recycled within the European Union. By 2036, this threshold shall rise to as least 40%.

ev.original: For schemes set up or updated from [OP: Please insert the date = 3 years after entry into force of this Regulation], the battery energy storage systems shall originate in the Union and contain battery cells, a battery management system as well as one additional main specific components that originate in the Union.
ev.amended: For schemes set up or updated from [OP: Please insert the date = 3 years after entry into force of this Regulation], the battery energy storage systems shall originate in the Union and contain battery cells, a battery management system, cathode active materials as well as one additional main specific components that originate in the Union. At least 20% of the relevant strategic raw materials used in batteries shall be mined, processed or recycled within the European Union. By 2036, this threshold shall rise to at least 40%.

(cb)Electric charging technologies for transport:
From [OP: Please insert the date = 2 years after entry into force of this Regulation], electric vehicle supply equipment, shore-side electricity supply equipment, and electric air transport supply equipment shall originate within the Union.

ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point a
ev.original: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;
ev.amended: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon and of Union origin; this percentage shall progressively rise according to the following: 25% from 1 January 2029, 35% from 1 January 2032, 50% from 1 January 2036.

ev.original: New pure electric vehicles (PEV), off-vehicle charging hybrid electric vehicles (OVC-HEV) or fuel cell vehicles (FCV) purchased, leased, rented or hire-purchased in public procurement procedures that fall within the scope of Directive 2014/24/EU, or Directive 2014/25/EU, launched on or after [OP: Please insert the date = six months after the date of entry into force of this Regulation] shall comply with the Union origin requirements set out in this Annex.
ev.amended: New pure electric vehicles (PEV), off-vehicle charging hybrid electric vehicles (OVC-HEV) or fuel cell vehicles (FCV) including heavy-duty vehicles, purchased, leased, rented or hire-purchased in public procurement procedures that fall within the scope of Directive 2014/24/EU, or Directive 2014/25/EU, launched on or after [OP: Please insert the date = six months after the date of entry into force of this Regulation] shall comply with the Union origin requirements set out in this Annex.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all components – excluding the battery – is at least 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all components – excluding the battery – is at least 75%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells and the binders, originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, including calcination and active material formation, the binders and the battery management system, originating in the Union; and at least 20% of the relevant strategic raw materials should be mined, processed or recycled within the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 5 – point 2 – point a
ev.original: (a)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%; or
ev.amended: (a)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 75%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 5 – point 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union.
ev.amended: (b)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the binders and the cathode active material, including calcination and active material formation, originating in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 75%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, and the binders, originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, including calcination and active material formation, the binders and the battery management system, originating in the Union; and at least 20% of the lithium used shall be mined, processed or reprocessed within the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 4 – point 2 – point a
ev.original: (a)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%; or
ev.amended: (a)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 75%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 4 – point 2 – point b

ev.amended: (b)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the binders and cathode active material, including calcination and active material formation, originating in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part III – paragraph 1 – point 2 – introductory part

ev.amended: 2.the two criteria below:

ev.amended: (a)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 75%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part III – paragraph 1 – point 2 – point b

ev.amended: (b)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the binders and cathode active material, including calcination and active material formation, originating in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part III – paragraph 1 – point 2 – point b – point 1 (new)
